newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money inches up to 11.5/12.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money inches up to 11.5/12.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money inched up to 11.5/12.0 percent from 10.0 percent on Tuesday morning due to some tightening of liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
One state bank dealer said the condition was mainly due to weekly tax payments due on Tuesday despite an early central bank injection of some 286 billion rupiah into the market.

She said early month tax payments were usually larger than those at the month-end. However, longer-term rates were quite stable, with one- and three-month money quoted at 13.00/13.25 and 14.00/14.25 percent, respectively.
Dealers said the relatively tight supply also caused tom/next swap to increase to 0.50/0.55 points from 0.40/0.45 points, indicating the market expected the tight conditions would continue.

The central bank offered one-week SBIs at 11.25 percent, two-week at 11.50 percent, one-month at 12.50 percent, three-month at 13.25 percent, six-month at 13.50 percent and 12-month at 13.75 percent on Monday.
Bond traders said prices were stable, with the benchmark PLN V/A bond still yielding 16.14 percent on Tuesday.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 9.59 percent, compared with 9.74 percent on Friday.
